paper_metadata.title: Quantum State Preparation by Improved MPS Method

summary: The paper proposes an improved MPS-based amplitude-preparation method (IMPS) with logarithmic circuit depth O(log n) versus conventional O(n) MPS depth, and a specific two-qubit-unitary optimization that reduces a fourth-order unitary from 3 CNOTs to 2. Numerical examples include 6-, 8-, and 12-qubit state-preparation benchmarks, with a 3x4 grid example showing 5 and 10 U-depths for the chip-adapted method versus 11 U-depths for traditional MPS.

experiments.description: Numerical evaluation of an improved MPS-based quantum state preparation method for amplitude encoding of six target functions/distributions, compared against standard MPS, TTN, HEN, and HTN connectivity schemes; includes a separate test of optimized two-CNOT decomposition for complex amplitudes and a scalability study versus qubit count.

algorithm.variant: Improved MPS (IMPS) state preparation / amplitude encoding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical functions/distributions are discretized into amplitudes of an n-qubit quantum state; the circuit approximately disentangles the target state to |0...0> and is then reversed for preparation. Qubits are paired arbitrarily or according to chip topology.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a target amplitude-encoded quantum state with high fidelity while minimizing circuit depth and two-qubit gate count.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Approximate truncation in MPS/TTN/HTN/HEN schemes; topology-aware disentangling on connected graphs; KAK/CSD-based two-qubit gate optimization for complex amplitudes.

problem_instance.description: Amplitude preparation for representative bounded-MPS-rank functions and benchmark distributions.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Functions/distributions are discretized into amplitudes; complex amplitudes are randomly generated for the unitary-optimization benchmark; fidelity averaged over 10 random samples per qubit count.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Infidelity and fidelity comparisons across methods; scalability evaluated as qubit number increases; repeated random-sample averaging for complex amplitudes.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Common superconducting quantum computer grid topology is discussed as an example; no specific transpilation target named
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: SVD-based recursive construction of disentangling unitaries; qubit reordering by binary indexing for HTN; graph contraction for arbitrary topologies.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Fidelity/infidelity computation and averaging over random samples.

speedup_claims.factor: O(log n) circuit depth vs conventional O(n) MPS depth
speedup_claims.conditions: unitary state preparation; without considering chip architecture
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is for approximate amplitude preparation and depends on bounded MPS rank / recursive disentangling.

speedup_claims.factor: approximately 33% reduction in two-qubit gate count
speedup_claims.baseline_method: standard fourth-order unitary decomposition requiring 3 CNOTs
speedup_claims.caveats: Applies to the specific fourth-order unitary decomposition used in the MPS framework.

speedup_claims.factor: approximately (m+n)/2 depth on an n x m grid
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a topology-specific scaling estimate, not a hardware benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log n) circuit depth for unitary IMPS preparation; approximately (m+n)/2 depth on an n x m grid; O(max(m,n)) for exact preparation of rank-2-or-less functions on grid chips

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Log-depth state-preparation circuits with O(log n) depth; example grid-topology depths of 5, 10, and 11 U-depths; two-CNOT decomposition instead of three CNOTs for a specific fourth-order unitary
limiting_factors: Results are numerical fidelity/infidelity comparisons only
No classical baseline that directly solves the same state-preparation task is evaluated
Advantage is a circuit-depth reduction, not a demonstrated end-to-end application speedup
Hardware connectivity and noise are discussed as constraints but not benchmarked on device

notes: No specific hardware execution is reported; hardware.type is not_specified because the paper presents numerical experiments and topology examples only.

num_qubits is inferred from the discussed examples (6-qubit figure, 8-qubit HTN example, 12-qubit grid-chip benchmark, and scalability plots) rather than a single explicit experiment-wide register size.
The paper reports theoretical and numerical improvements in circuit depth and CNOT count, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical methods.
